decisions.reason: The indoor air quality Bricklet was launched recently, has its own page, and costs little to keep in a modular catalog while demand for air quality sensing is still unfolding, so the option is worth holding.
The Analog In Bricklet 3.0 is the current generation replacing version 2.0, so it is a core building block whose value is fairly secure and whose carrying cost is low.
The MQTT proxy is a software binding with almost no marginal cost, and it widens the platform's reach into IoT use cases whose value is still developing.
The CAN bus interface is a new connectivity module with uncertain but plausible industrial and automotive demand, and keeping a low-cost module in the catalog preserves that upside.
The CO2 sensor Bricklet has its own page and serves growing ventilation and education demand, so the option has not resolved negatively and is cheap to keep.
The touch panel accessory is cheap to keep listed and complements display modules, and its value is still uncertain, though accessories face a somewhat higher risk of being phased out.
